Th ese eﬀ ects demonstrate the importance of insulin in tissue 
growth.1, 4
Glucagon Glucagon is the hormone released from alpha
cells of the pancreas when blood glucose levels fall below the 
normal range, necessitating a source of energy to maintain 
homeostasis. Glucagon stimulates the breakdown of stored gly-
cogen (glycogenolysis) and the production of new glucose from
amino acids (gluconeogenesis), and thus raises blood glucose.
Glucagon also stimulates lipolysis, which provides additional 
substrate to meet energy requirements.
